identification.summary: Periwinkle Tempest (formerly DEV-0193, also called Trickbot LLC) is a financially motivated cybercriminal group that Microsoft says develops, distributes and manages many different payloads, including Trickbot, BazaLoader and AnchorDNS [S1][S2]. Microsoft says it ran the Ryuk ransomware-as-a-service operation until Ryuk shut down in June 2021, then ran Ryuk's successor Conti and also Diavol [S1][S2]. Microsoft calls it the most prolific ransomware-associated cybercriminal activity group active today [S1][S2]. Microsoft also says it hired developers from Emotet, Qakbot and IcedID as those operations shut down [S1][S2]. In May 2025 Germany's BKA publicly named Vitaly Nikolaevich Kovalev ('Stern') as the suspected founder of the Trickbot group (also known as Wizard Spider) and said the group at times had more than 100 members [S8].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft has tracked the group since October 2020 [S1][S2]. The September 2023 US Trickbot indictment alleges a conspiracy beginning in November 2015 (reporting the DOJ indictment) [S7].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Periwinkle Tempest (formerly DEV-0193; also Trickbot LLC) [S1]. Microsoft tracks DEV-0365 as a subgroup of DEV-0193 that provides Cobalt Strike Beacon infrastructure as a service to other criminals [S2]. Microsoft tracks the Conti/Ryuk affiliate DEV-0237 (now Pistachio Tempest) and the Conti Manual author DEV-0230 as separate actors that bought access or payloads from DEV-0193 [S2]. Mandiant's FIN12 (formerly UNC1878) is a Ryuk-deploying affiliate cluster that relied on partners, originally TrickBot, for initial access [S9]. FIN12 is a vendor cluster and is not stated by any cited source to be the same as Periwinkle Tempest. The BKA uses 'Trickbot group' and 'Wizard Spider' interchangeably [S8].

attribution.sponsor: No state sponsor. The group is a Russia-based criminal enterprise [S6][S8]. US Treasury said in February 2023 that sanctioned Trickbot members had close links to Russia's intelligence services, and that the group's preparations in 2020 aligned with Russian state objectives and with targeting previously conducted by Russian Intelligence Services (reporting Treasury press release) [S6].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft attributes the Trickbot, BazaLoader, AnchorDNS, Ryuk, Conti and Diavol operations to Periwinkle Tempest/DEV-0193 by name [S1][S2]. The US and UK governments sanctioned seven alleged Trickbot members in February 2023 and eleven more in September 2023 (reporting Treasury/FCDO actions) [S6][S7]. The US unsealed criminal indictments in September 2023 (reporting DOJ) [S7]. The BKA named the alleged leader in May 2025 [S8]. The Treasury link to Russian intelligence is an assessment of alignment, not a statement that the state directs the group [S6].
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and threat intelligence [S1][S2]; US/UK sanctions designations [S6]; US federal indictments in the Northern District of Ohio, Middle District of Tennessee and Southern District of California (reporting DOJ) [S7]; German BKA investigation under Operation Endgame [S8].

objectives: Financial gain through banking-malware fraud, the sale of access and payloads, and big-game ransomware extortion [S1][S2][S7]. The Trickbot indictment alleges a conspiracy to use Trickbot to steal money and confidential information (reporting DOJ) [S7].

sectors: Government, including national ministries and local law enforcement and emergency medical services [S7][S10]
targeting.notes: Microsoft names education and healthcare as targeted industries [S1]. CISA, FBI and HHS warned in October 2020 of an increased and imminent Ryuk/Trickbot threat to US hospitals (reporting AA20-302A) [S3]. Mandiant reported that FIN12, a Ryuk affiliate cluster, disproportionately targeted healthcare and large organizations, usually with revenue above $300 million [S9]; FIN12 is a separate vendor cluster.

capabilities.summary: Develops and runs a loader and botnet ecosystem (Trickbot, BazaLoader, AnchorDNS) that serves as an initial-access source for its own and others' ransomware operations [S1][S2]. Microsoft says DEV-0193 infrastructure was implicated in exploitation of CVE-2021-40444 [S2]. Its DEV-0365 subgroup provides Cobalt Strike Beacon infrastructure as a service [S2]. The BKA lists Bazarloader, SystemBC, IcedID, Ryuk, Conti and Diavol in the group's alleged toolkit [S8]. The 2020 CISA/FBI/HHS advisory says Ryuk was typically deployed as a payload after banking trojans such as Trickbot (reporting AA20-302A) [S3]. In the 2021 HSE intrusion, the PwC post-incident review found initial access came through a malicious Excel attachment in a phishing email on 16 March 2021, about two months before Conti was deployed [S5].

campaigns.name: Trickbot fraud conspiracy (alleged start)
campaigns.summary: The US indictment alleges a conspiracy to use Trickbot to steal money and confidential information beginning in November 2015 (reporting DOJ).

campaigns.name: Trickbot botnet disruption
campaigns.summary: Microsoft used an Eastern District of Virginia court order to take down Trickbot C2 servers, citing election security risk. Reporting indicated only part of the botnet was taken down.

campaigns.name: Ryuk wave against US hospitals
campaigns.summary: CISA, FBI and HHS issued AA20-302A warning of an increased and imminent Ryuk/Trickbot threat to US healthcare providers.

campaigns.name: Ireland Health Service Executive (Conti)
campaigns.summary: Conti ransomware forced a nationwide shutdown of HSE IT systems. Initial access was a phishing email on 16 March 2021, and full server decryption took until September 2021.

campaigns.name: Ryuk retired; Conti and Diavol continue
campaigns.summary: Microsoft says DEV-0193 managed Ryuk until its June 2021 shutdown, then its successor Conti and Diavol.

campaigns.name: Costa Rica government attack (Conti)
campaigns.summary: Conti breached Costa Rica's Finance Ministry on 12 April 2022 and hit other agencies. A national emergency was declared on 8 May 2022.

campaigns.name: Conti deployments cease
campaigns.summary: Microsoft observed no Conti deployments after 19 April 2022, suggesting the program had shut down or paused.

campaigns.name: First US/UK Trickbot sanctions
campaigns.summary: Seven alleged Trickbot members, including Vitaly Kovalev, were sanctioned. Treasury cited links to Russian intelligence services (reporting Treasury).

campaigns.name: Second sanctions round and indictments
campaigns.summary: Eleven more alleged members were sanctioned, and Trickbot and Conti indictments in Ohio, Tennessee and California were unsealed (reporting DOJ/Treasury).

campaigns.name: BKA names 'Stern' (Operation Endgame)
campaigns.summary: Germany's BKA identified Vitaly Nikolaevich Kovalev as the suspected Trickbot founder 'Stern' and sought him under an Interpol red notice. He is believed to be in Russia.

diamond.adversary: Russia-based cybercriminal enterprise of more than 100 members at times; suspected founder Vitaly Kovalev ('Stern') [S8]; sanctioned and indicted members [S6][S7].
diamond.capability: Trickbot, BazaLoader, AnchorDNS, IcedID and SystemBC loaders; Ryuk, Conti and Diavol ransomware; Cobalt Strike Beacon via the DEV-0365 subgroup; CVE-2021-40444 exploitation [S1][S2][S8].
diamond.infrastructure: Trickbot botnet C2 servers (disrupted in 2020) [S4]; Cobalt Strike Beacon infrastructure offered as a service [S2]; phishing email delivery [S5].
diamond.victim: Healthcare and education [S1]; US hospitals [S3]; Ireland's HSE [S5]; Costa Rican government ministries [S10]; US businesses, nonprofits, police, sheriff and EMS organizations [S7].
diamond.socioPolitical: Profit-driven extortion from a safe haven in Russia; Treasury assessed in 2020 that the group's preparations aligned with Russian state objectives [S6][S8].
diamond.technology: Windows enterprise networks reached through malicious Office documents and loader botnets; disruption of hospital and government IT services [S3][S5][S10].

gaps: Primary documents not opened: Treasury press releases (Feb and Sep 2023), the DOJ indictments, CISA AA20-302A and the BKA release. Facts come from press or trade-association coverage of them.

Microsoft cluster boundary: Periwinkle Tempest (DEV-0193) runs the payloads, while affiliates such as DEV-0237/Pistachio Tempest and DEV-0230 deployed them [S2]. Which specific incidents (HSE, Costa Rica) Microsoft attributes to Periwinkle Tempest's own operators, rather than to Conti affiliates, is not stated in the sources gathered.

This record's aliases include FIN12/UNC1878 (Mandiant), which Mandiant describes as a Ryuk affiliate that relied on partners for access [S9]. That may overlap more with Microsoft's affiliate clusters than with Periwinkle Tempest. Equivalence is unverified.
Microsoft also lists Storm-0230 as a 'Wizard Spider/Conti Team 1' development group (per the record's import notes). The relationship to Periwinkle Tempest is not documented in the sources gathered.
Activity after Conti's 2022 shutdown (successor brands, current loader operations) is not documented in sources gathered beyond the 2025 BKA action.
The nature and extent of any Russian intelligence tasking is unverified beyond Treasury's alignment statement [S6].
Microsoft's Security Insider profile gives no origin or targeted regions [S1].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Defense health facilities, education and installation-support networks that depend on commercial and local-government services fall within the operational environment, given the healthcare, education and local-government victimology [S1][S3][S7]. STEP 2: Loader botnets (Trickbot, BazaLoader, IcedID) feed affiliate ransomware. Phishing-to-ransomware dwell time can be weeks, as in the HSE intrusion (about two months) [S2][S5]. Law-enforcement takedowns have degraded the operation only partly and temporarily [S4]. STEP 3: The doctrinal template is a phishing Office document, then a loader, then Cobalt Strike Beacon, then domain-wide ransomware with data theft [S2][S3][S5]. STEP 4: MLCOA is opportunistic ransomware extortion against healthcare, education or local-government enablers of military installations through affiliates using this group's loaders. MDCOA is a coordinated wave against hospitals or national government services during a crisis, as in the 2020 US hospital warning and the 2022 Costa Rica emergency [S3][S10]. The MDCOA might be timed to align with Russian state interests [S6]. Candidate indicators: Trickbot/BazaLoader/IcedID detections, Cobalt Strike Beacon C2 associated with DEV-0365 infrastructure, CVE-2021-40444 exploitation attempts, and malicious Excel or Word attachments [S2][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. SITUATIONAL AWARENESS: Loader infections are precursors to ransomware, so treat loader detections on DODIN-adjacent or mission-partner networks as pre-ransomware warnings [S2][S3]. AUTHORITIES: This is a criminal actor under US/UK sanctions and indictment [S6][S7]. Response is chiefly law-enforcement and DCO-led, with private-sector disruption precedent [S4]. Coordinate with the FBI, CISA and HHS for health-sector cases [S3]. MISSION ASSURANCE: Hospital, EMS and local-government dependencies were disrupted for weeks to months [S5][S10]. Plan for degraded medical and civil support to installations. COORDINATION: Multinational action (US, UK, Germany/Operation Endgame) supports information sharing with allied law enforcement [S6][S8].
